_about: Which side of a dedicated-server setup each mod belongs on, so deploy-dathost.ps1 only
uploads what can actually run there and mod-status.ps1 stops reporting a client-only mod as
client  - never upload. The server has no use for it.
server  - upload; the server needs it and clients do not.
both    - upload, and clients need it too.
The authority for 'client' is usually the code itself: [BepInProcess("valheim.exe")] on the
plugin class makes BepInEx skip the plugin entirely under valheim_server.exe, so such a DLL
cannot run on the server no matter where it is copied. mod-status.ps1 cross-checks this file
against that attribute and reports any mod whose declared side contradicts its own code.
'profilePackages' covers the third-party packages mirrored by deploy-dathost.ps1 -Profile,
keyed by the package folder name as it appears in the Gale profile's BepInEx/plugins. Only
list one when it should be skipped or forced; anything absent is mirrored as before.

Armory.why: Was client, changed 2026-09-15. Adds a new prefab (armory_rack). ZNetScene.CreateObjectsSorted does not merely skip a ZDO it cannot instantiate - on the server it takes ownership and calls ZDOMan.DestroyZDO - so a server without the mod permanently deletes racks built inside its own active area, which never leaves the world center, along with their contents and saved loadouts. Same failure ForsakenShrines had. The server also needs it to answer the container's open request and the rack's ArmoryRPC_SetData for racks it owns. The [BepInProcess("valheim.exe")] gate is gone as of 1.2.0.

CaptainsLog.why: Was client, changed 2026-09-17 in 1.1.0: the [BepInProcess] gate is gone. Clients log their own sailing without the server copy; on a dedicated server it logs every player's sailing to BepInEx/CaptainsLog/shiplog-server-*.csv. It adds no prefab and no RPC, so a server without it breaks nothing.

DiagnoseServerLag.why: The server half is the point: it measures its own tick times and per-player socket state and answers clients over a routed RPC. A client cannot make that measurement for itself, so without the server copy the mod can never rule the server in or out.

DudeWhatAreMyStats.why: Was client, changed 2026-09-15. Players who are online still answer for themselves over a routed RPC, which needs nothing on the server. The server half is what remembers players who are NOT online: it keeps each character's last known stats under BepInEx/config/DudeWhatAreMyStats/ and hands them out on request. Without it on the server that feature is simply absent, so uploading is optional but the scoreboard is half a scoreboard otherwise.

ForsakenShrines.why: Adds new prefabs (shrine_*). A server without them deletes the ZDOs it cannot instantiate near the world center, and ServerSync has nothing to enforce from. The client gate was the bug and is gone as of 0.8.3.

GrabMaterials.why: [BepInProcess("valheim.exe")] - reads and moves the local player's inventory.

PauseMyServer.why: Server-authoritative: the server decides whether a pause is granted and broadcasts it; the client freezes.

TheGreatestMap.why: The shared marker store and the live portal list come from the server, and deploy-dathost.ps1's pre-stop world save depends on this mod's save-now trigger running there.

TheGreatestPortal.why: README: install on the server and on every client.

TheGreatestShips.why: Adds new ship prefabs (DM_FastKarve, DM_FastLongship, DM_CargoLongship). A server without them deletes the ZDOs it cannot instantiate near the world center, and the sail force and recipe are server-synced config.

_profileNote: Third-party packages in the Gale 'Default SD' profile, audited 2026-09-14 from the author's
Thunderstore categories, the package README, and what the mod does.
DO NOT classify a third-party mod by scanning its DLL for a "valheim.exe" string. That was the
first method used here and it put Crystal-Pathfinder on the client-only list, which got it
deleted off the server even though its README says to install it on both. The string and the
BepInProcess type both appear in DLLs that are not gated at all. Reading the attribute off
source is reliable, which is why the mods in this repo can be judged that way and these cannot.
For a package with no Client-side or Server-side category, read its README before deciding -
Pathfinder had no side category and that absence was the real signal that it needed checking.
A Thunderstore 'Server-side' category usually means the mod CAN be installed server-side so its
config is authoritative and synced, not that the server needs it. Those are marked 'both' where
the server genuinely participates and 'optional-server' where installing it there only buys
enforced config - the deploy uploads those, since that is the status quo, but they are the ones
to prune if the server is ever under load.
'unknown' means it needs a look: the deploy treats it as before (uploaded) and nothing is
deleted on that basis.
A package on the server that is in no Gale profile is NOT automatically stale. Some are there
on purpose because the server is the only place they do anything, and they have no local copy
to re-upload. Check this file before deleting anything off the server, and if a package is not
listed here, ask rather than assume - that shape got PortalRules and OttoFuel deleted, and
those were only meant to go because Greg said so.
'excluded' is a decision rather than a capability: the mod could run on the server, but it is
deliberately not wanted there. Deploys skip it exactly as they skip 'client', so it does not
come back on the next profile mirror. Nothing carries it at the moment.
A package disabled in the Gale profile is disabled for one of two reasons: something replaced
it, or it has not been updated for Valheim 1.0 yet. Neither is a reason to send it to the
server. Not coming back: OdinShipPlus, dropped by Greg on 2026-09-16 and
removed from the server and every profile - it was hand-installed with no namespace, so Gale's
uninstall never saw its folder; BadgersValheimSkies, part of the Wallybach
and Badger HD set, client-only and dropped from this file entirely; and PortalRules and
OttoFuel, both replaced by alternatives and removed from the server on 2026-09-14 - their
orphaned config still sits under BepInEx/config there, including PortalRules' player-identities
and cooldown data, which is why it was not deleted with the plugins.

Sfantul-PortalGhostFix.why: SERVER ONLY - DO NOT DELETE. Installed straight onto the server on 2026-09-15 and deliberately in no Gale profile, which makes it look exactly like the server-only leftovers (PortalRules, OttoFuel) deleted on 2026-09-14 for being in no profile. It is not a leftover. Nothing here can put it back either: there is no local copy, and the only source is https://thunderstore.io/c/valheim/p/Sfantul/PortalGhostFix/. Its DLL is PortalObserverFix.dll, which does not match the package name, so a check keyed on either name will miss the other.

Crystal-Pathfinder.why: CORRECTED 2026-09-14 (was wrongly client): its README says 'This mod should be installed on client and server', and a server running it rejects clients without it unless ConditionalConfigSync's ModRequirements.cfg says otherwise. It was deleted from the server in the 14 Sep sweep on bad evidence and restored the same night.

Neobotics-GetComfortable.why: A comfort HUD overlay. No server install mentioned anywhere in its README.

Neobotics-HUDCompass.why: A heads-up compass drawn on the player's screen. No server install mentioned in its README.

Neobotics-QuietPortals.why: Portal volume and activation distance; Client-side on Thunderstore.

Stonaar-ValheimSkipIntro.why: Skips the startup cinematic. Nothing for a headless server to skip.

Advize-PlantEasily.why: Client-side only on Thunderstore. Planting grid is a placement UI.

Azumatt-AzuWorkbench_Inventory_Repair.why: Client-side only. Disabled in the profile.

Azumatt-Official_BepInEx_ConfigurationMa.why: An in-game settings window; a headless server has no UI. Disabled in the profile.

ComfyMods-BetterZeeLog.why: Client-side on Thunderstore. Worth revisiting if server-side ZLog output is ever wanted.

ComfyMods-ReportCard.why: Client-side only. Disabled in the profile; its stats panel broke on Valheim 1.0.

JereKuusela-Render_Limits.why: Rendering limits are a client concern; the Server-side tag is for config sync. Disabled in the profile.

LTmadness-GumshoeTimerSuite.why: Client-side only. Timers drawn on processors.

MSchmoecker-ContentsWithin.why: Client-side only. Disabled in the profile.

Zenox-ServerConnect.why: A main-menu connect button; meaningless on a server.

shudnal-ConfigurationManager.why: An in-game settings window. Tagged Server-side, but a headless server has no UI.

shudnal-MyLittleUI.why: UI tweaks. Tagged Server-side for config sync only.

CW_Jesse-BetterNetworking_Valheim.why: Compresses and paces the network protocol; both ends must agree.

shudnal-ConditionalConfigSync.why: Config synchronization and server policy library - the server is where policy lives.

ValheimModding-JsonDotNET.why: Shared library a server-side mod may load.

ValheimModding-YamlDotNet.why: Shared library a server-side mod may load.

Azumatt-AzuAutoStore.why: Client feature; Server-side tag buys enforced config.

Azumatt-AzuCraftyBoxes.why: Client pulls from containers; server install enforces the config.

Azumatt-AzuExtendedPlayerInventory.why: Client inventory UI; server install enforces the config.

Azumatt-Recycle_N_Reclaim.why: Recipes are resolved client-side; server install enforces the config.

Azumatt-RepairStation.why: Check whether it registers a new prefab - if it does, it is 'both'.

Shalopay-FoodSorting.why: Client-only. Disabled because it does not work on Valheim 1.0; Greg will re-enable it if that is ever fixed.

SmartSilencer.why: [BepInProcess("valheim.exe")]. Scales the local AudioListener from Windows per-app level meters and window focus; a dedicated server has neither sound nor a window.
